field.label: Enable failover monitor
field.help: Turn the FRITZ!Box failover monitor on. When it detects a broken cable line it makes OPNsense switch to your backup gateway (e.g. 5G/LTE) and switches back automatically once the cable line works again.

field.label: Test mode (dry run)
field.help: Runs all checks and records every lost ping per test address, but NEVER changes anything on OPNsense. The status shows what the plugin would have done ("would fail over"). Leave this on for a few days to see whether the test addresses also suffer from the timeouts you see with dpinger, then switch it off to activate the failover. Switching test mode on also restores the normal monitor IP if a real failover is active.

field.label: How to detect a dead cable line
field.help: "FRITZ!Box status" reads whether the FRITZ!Box has an internet connection. It notices a lost cable sync or a lost IP address, but NOT a Vodafone backbone outage (the FRITZ!Box keeps saying "Connected" then). The "internet ping check" additionally pings the test addresses below directly through the cable line and detects such outages. Recommended: both.

field.label: FRITZ!Box IP address
field.help: The address of your FRITZ!Box as seen from OPNsense. For a Vodafone FRITZ!Box 6660 Cable this is usually 192.168.0.1 (or 192.168.178.1).

field.label: TR-064 / UPnP port
field.help: Port of the FRITZ!Box for TR-064 and UPnP status requests. Leave this at 49000.

field.label: TR-064 username (optional)
field.help: Leave empty (recommended) to read the status via UPnP without any login: enable "Transmit status information over UPnP" on the FRITZ!Box (Home Network > Network > Network Settings). Only if that is not possible, enter a dedicated FRITZ!Box user for TR-064 ("Allow access for applications" must be enabled); after a failed login, TR-064 is paused for 15 minutes to avoid a FRITZ!Box login lockout.

field.label: TR-064 password (optional)
field.help: Password of the TR-064 user above. It is stored in the OPNsense configuration (like all passwords there) and never written to log files.

field.label: Cable gateway name
field.help: The cable gateway from System > Gateways > Configuration. Pick it from the list; only saved gateways can be managed (automatically created ones such as WAN_DHCP must be opened and saved once). Its monitor IP is changed automatically by this plugin.

field.label: Backup gateway (optional)
field.help: The backup gateway (e.g. the 5G/LTE line). Only used for notifications: the public IP in the failover message is looked up through this line. Leave empty if you do not use Pushover.

field.label: Cable interface
field.help: The OPNsense interface connected to the FRITZ!Box (e.g. WAN on vtnet5). The test pings use the address of this interface as source, so OPNsense always sends them through the cable line, even during a failover. Leave on "Automatic" to use the interface of the gateway above.

field.label: Normal monitor IP
field.help: The IP the OPNsense gateway monitor (dpinger) pings while the cable line is fine. Use the FRITZ!Box address (e.g. 192.168.0.1, the same as the gateway): it is always reachable, so the gateway monitor never raises a false alarm. Whether the internet really works is decided by this plugin, not by the gateway monitor.

field.label: Fake monitor IP (failover)
field.help: An address that never answers. When the cable line fails the monitor IP is switched to this one, which makes OPNsense see 100% loss and fail over. 192.0.2.1 (reserved documentation range) is the safe default.

field.label: Internet test addresses
field.help: Public addresses that are pinged through the cable line (in parallel, max. 5). The line only counts as dead if NONE of them answers, so a single unreachable server never triggers a failover. Enter at least two (better three) addresses of different providers. Default: 9.9.9.9, 1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8.

field.label: Check interval (seconds)
field.help: How often the cable line is checked. Default: 10 seconds.

field.label: Pings per check
field.help: Number of test pings sent to each test address per check. Default: 2.

field.label: Ping timeout (seconds)
field.help: How long to wait for each ping answer. Default: 2 seconds.

field.label: Failures before failover
field.help: Number of failed checks in a row before switching to the backup line. Higher values avoid switching on short hiccups. Default: 3.

field.label: Successes before switching back
field.help: Number of successful checks in a row before switching back to cable. Prevents flapping while the line is unstable. Default: 3.

field.label: Regular self-healing restart
field.help: Restarts only this plugin's own monitor process at the chosen time and clears its runtime files (counters, temporary files). Statistics and switch history are kept. OPNsense, routing, firewall and dpinger are not touched. For safety it only happens while everything is fine (state "Cable line OK"); during a failover, a test failover, while failures are being counted or while a notification/DNS update is pending it is postponed to the next time slot. Recommended: on, daily.

field.label: Self-healing interval
field.help: Daily, or weekly on Sunday.

field.label: Self-healing hour
field.help: Hour of the day (0-23, local time of the firewall) in which the restart takes place. Default: 4 (between 04:00 and 04:59).

field.label: Switch DNS record on failover
field.help: Points a DNS record (e.g. the WireGuard host name your clients connect to) to the backup line during a failover and back to the cable line afterwards, so remote clients follow automatically. Uses the Cloudflare API. Only done on real switches (and test failovers), never in test mode.

field.label: Cloudflare API token
field.help: A Cloudflare user API token. Create it at dash.cloudflare.com > My Profile > API Tokens > Create Token > Create Custom Token with exactly these permissions: Zone - Zone - Read and Zone - DNS - Edit. Under Zone Resources choose Include - Specific zone - your domain (e.g. domain.com). No other permissions are needed. Do not use the Global API Key.

field.label: Record to switch (CNAME)
field.help: The host name your clients use, e.g. wg.domain.com. It is set as a CNAME (DNS only, not proxied; WireGuard cannot run through the Cloudflare proxy). If it does not exist yet it is created; an existing A/AAAA record with this name is not touched, delete it first.

field.label: Normal destination
field.help: Where the record points while the cable line works, e.g. fritz-cable.domain.com (kept up to date by the dynamic DNS of the cable FRITZ!Box).

field.label: Failover destination
field.help: Where the record points during a failover, e.g. fritz-5g.domain.com (dynamic DNS of the backup line).

field.label: TTL (seconds)
field.help: Time to live of the record. 60 seconds (the minimum at Cloudflare) lets clients follow a switch within about a minute.

field.label: Send push notifications
field.help: Sends a Pushover message when OPNsense switches to the backup line (and back). Only done on real switches (and test failovers), never in test mode.

field.label: Pushover API token
field.help: The API token of a Pushover application: pushover.net > Your Applications > Create an Application/API Token, e.g. named "OPNsense".

field.label: Pushover user key
field.help: Your user key (shown on the pushover.net start page after login) or a group key.

field.label: Public IP services
field.help: Web services that return your public IPv4 address as plain text; the address is added to every message. They are asked in this order until one answers, always via IPv4. Enter at least two, in case one is down. Default: https://ifconfig.me/ip and https://ip.me.

field.label: Notification delay (seconds)
field.help: Extra wait after OPNsense reported the switch before the message is sent, so routing has settled and the public IP of the new line is shown. 3 to 30 seconds, default 5.

field.label: Also notify when switching back
field.help: Also send a message when the cable line is used again.
